_about: Per-work Blau overlay for Maimonides' Guide (Moreh Nevukhim), Part I ch. 1. Rendered ONLY in /advanced/moreh, so a special Judaeo-Arabic sense surfaced here never bleeds into the Kuzari, Bahya, or Saadia readers. Source: Joshua Blau, A Dictionary of Medieval Judaeo-Arabic Texts (Jerusalem 2006). NOTE: Blau rarely cites the Guide itself (his Maimonides material is mostly the Responsa and Mishnah-commentary); these are Blau-attested medieval-JA senses for words that occur in this text, not Guide-specific citations.

notes.blau_sense_en: In medieval Judaeo-Arabic, maʿnā ranges well beyond classical 'meaning': Blau records the post-classical senses 'reason, intent', 'shape, form', and 'subject, matter, a thing'. In the Guide it is Maimonides' technical word for the intelligible notion or concept a name denotes — here, that the 'image of God' names the human's rational notion, not a bodily shape.
notes.attested_in: Blau, Dict. of Medieval Judaeo-Arabic (post-classical senses)

notes.blau_sense_en: Besides 'shape, figure', Blau records the medieval-JA senses 'sort, kind, manner' and even 'script, writing'. The Guide turns on the contrast between shakl (mere outward shape/figure) and ṣūra (the essential 'form') — the multitude wrongly take 'image' to mean the former.
